brief: Calmly receive a potentially embarrassing fact without collapsing, arguing, or performing dominance.

line: Accept the fact. Do not automatically accept the shame.
brief: Separate useful information from the social humiliation someone tried to attach to it.
Evidence, experiment, or the world itself outranks rhetoric, prestige, and applause.

section: A good idea must be allowed to fail
line: A good idea must be allowed to fail.
brief: A real test has a visible path to failure; a protected idea is theater rather than inquiry.

section: This philosophy may also be wrong
line: Do not defend something merely because it is yours.
brief: Release attachment to one's own idea when reality supplies a better one.
Disagreement need not imply stupidity, jealousy, corruption, fear, or malice.

section: Reputation and truth are different questions
line: What is true? is different from How does this make me look?
brief: Visually separate truth-seeking from reputation management without making either invisible.

section: Build tools that can disagree with you
line: Build tools that can say no to you.
brief: A useful instrument, experiment, friend, or computer can contradict its creator.

section: Keep track of where things came from
line: Keep the receipts. Then check the claim.
brief: Preserve provenance and attribution while still testing the object itself.
Exploration can be ridiculous and joyful when the boundary between play and assertion stays visible.

line: More words are not necessarily more wisdom.
brief: Stop elaborating after the useful distinction is already held.

line: There is no special step called: Become defensive.
brief: When a claim arrives: yes if true, show why if false, test if uncertain, and continue.
